Passage VI
Nuclear fusion is the process by which 2 nuclei
combine to form a single, more massive nucleus. In this
process, 1 or more subatomic particles (such as a proton, p,
or a neutron, n) may also be produced. A teacher asked her
students to consider the following 2 nuclear reactions.
Reaction 1:
H
H
He
Reaction 2:
H
H
He
n
Each reactant and product has 2 numbers associated
with it: a mass number (the number on top) and an atomic
number (the number on the bottom). Further, the atomic
number indicates the positive charge. The teacher then
asked the students to determine which of the reactions, if
either, can occur.
Student 1
For a fusion reaction to occur, mass number and
atomic number must both be conserved. (A conserved
quantity is one whose value does not change during a
reaction.) In both Reaction 1 and Reaction 2, the sum
of the mass numbers of the reactants is equal to the sum
of the mass numbers of the products. Similarly, the sum of
the atomic numbers of the reactants is equal to the sum of
the atomic numbers of the products. Thus, mass number
and atomic number are both conserved in both reactions,
so both reactions can occur.
Student 2
Student 1 is correct; however, in addition, if each
reactant is positively charged, each product must also be
positively charged. The product of Reaction 1 is positively
charged, but the products of Reaction 2 include a neutral
particle. Thus, Reaction 1 can occur, but Reaction 2
cannot.
Student 3
For a fusion reaction to occur, mass number and
electric charge must both be conserved, and there must be
at least 2 products. Though mass number and electric
charge are both conserved in both reactions, Reaction 1
has only 1 product. Thus, Reaction 2 can occur, but
Reaction 1 cannot.
Student 4
For a fusion reaction to occur, electric charge must be
conserved, there must be at least 2 products, and if each
reactant is positively charged, each product must also be
positively charged. Thus, neither Reaction 1 nor
Reaction 2 can occur.
Following the students’ responses, the teacher
provided them with 2 example reactions (Reactions Y and
Z) that can both occur.
Reaction Y:
He
He
He
p
p
Reaction Z:
H
H
He
n
